answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks with a decaying-reward stake bond. Each agent identity must lock a bond far above the epoch payout, so cloning stays unprofitable: rewards shrink for every new identity sharing one funding ancestor, driving marginal profit to its nadir and making a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds. Each identity also needs a beacon, an attestation from an established node staking its own collateral on the newcomer, slashed on fraud. During an early zephyr phase identities carry tiny weight, so a flood of clones cannot sweep the ledger.
